spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (any: fatal error raised -> matching Error + Close)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §6.2 (revocation-driven close of an active session uses 204 within <= 5 s)
description: Revocation of a live session: the operator revokes the Client identity while its session is PLAYING; within <= 5 s the session receives the fatal pair Error(204)+Close(204).
preconditions: Session authenticated by the (now revoked) identity; state PLAYING with an active stream (session_id 1).
The authorization store changed under the session; Server Core watches the authorization-state generation (pairing.md §9.2).
assertions: Unsolicited Error: request_id 0 (proto3 default, not encoded) — no request is being answered.
Fatal pairing: Error+Close with the same code; the transport close carries 204 as well (spec §3).
The close reason is in the pairing/authorization-failure category — non-retryable without admin action (pairing.md §9.2, spec §6.3).
Note: the §5.2 supersede row (303) names Close alone; this revocation path has no such row and therefore follows the generic fatal-error row (Error + Close).
